newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: C.BANK GOVERNOR SAYS TAURAS BANK INSOLVENT.
newsitem.headline: C.BANK GOVERNOR SAYS TAURAS BANK INSOLVENT.

text.p: Bank of Lithuania Governor Reinoldijus Sharkinas said on Monday that investigations had confirmed that Tauras Bank was insolvent and that the board of the central bank would discuss it on Tuesday.
"People have been working during the days off and we can say that the bank is really insolvent," Sharkinas said at a news conference.
Sharkinas said that central bank inspectors had finished their investigations into Tauras.
"Now we are looking for the candidature of an administrator," Sharkinas added. "We plan to have a board meeting tomorrow morning, and we will discuss these issues during the meeting."
Sharkinas did not rule out the possibility of another audit into Tauras.
The central bank removed the board of Tauras Bank earlier this month and imposed restrictions on most of its activities after it ran into a liquidity crunch.
Tauras admitted last month that it was having serious liquidity problems and was pinning its hopes of survival on a 40 million litas share issue.
Lithuania was rocked by a banking crisis in late 1995 with the shock closure of two of its top banks but analysts say the sector has recovered and do not expect Tauras' troubles to spread.
The bank has a limited number of corporate and business clients and so the political impact of its problems has been minimised.
In a grim twist to the tale, the bank's president, Genadijus Konopliovas, was found dead last Monday with a bullet wound to the head. Police say he killed himself.
Konopliovas was also one of the main owners of the bank.
